name: Hampi
description: The ruins of Vijayanagara-era Hampi preserve monumental temples, markets and urban architecture across a dramatic boulder landscape.
significance: A major cultural and architectural landscape associated with the Vijayanagara Empire.

name: Ajanta Caves
description: Rock-cut Buddhist caves containing celebrated murals, sculptures and monastic spaces.
significance: Important evidence of Indian Buddhist art, architecture and painting traditions.
indoor: Site interpretation spaces and museum facilities

name: Ellora Caves
description: A monumental complex of Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut architecture.
significance: Demonstrates religious coexistence and sophisticated rock-cut engineering.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A monumental temple complex conceived in the form of a chariot dedicated to the Sun god.
significance: Renowned for its stone carving, iconography and architectural conception.

name: Sanchi Stupa
description: A historic Buddhist complex known for stupas, gateways and monastic remains.
significance: One of the major surviving Buddhist architectural landscapes in India.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: A group of medieval Hindu and Jain temples distinguished by detailed stone sculpture and architectural composition.
significance: A major expression of medieval Indian temple art and architecture.

name: Red Fort
description: A Mughal-era fortified palace complex built in red sandstone and associated with the history of Delhi.
significance: A landmark of Mughal architecture and modern India's national history.
indoor: Museums and interpretation areas within the complex

name: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
description: A coastal group of rock-cut caves, monolithic rathas and structural temples associated with the Pallava period.
significance: Important evidence of early South Indian architectural experimentation in stone.

name: Taj Mahal
description: A white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, combining Persian, Islamic and Indian architectural styles.
significance: Widely regarded as the finest example of Mughal architecture and a symbol of India's cultural heritage.

name: Qutub Minar
description: A soaring five-storey minaret of fluted red sandstone and marble, begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by his successors.
significance: The tallest brick minaret in the world and an early landmark of Indo-Islamic architecture.

name: Fatehpur Sikri
description: A planned Mughal city built by Emperor Akbar as his capital, featuring palaces, courts and the Jama Masjid complex in red sandstone.
significance: An exceptionally well-preserved example of Mughal urban planning and architecture.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: The garden-tomb of Emperor Humayun, built by his widow Bega Begum, notable for its charbagh garden layout and monumental scale.
significance: The first grand dynastic mausoleum in India and a direct architectural precursor to the Taj Mahal.

name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
description: A monumental granite temple built by the Chola king Raja Raja I, part of the Great Living Chola Temples group.
significance: A pinnacle of Dravidian temple architecture and Chola engineering, crowned by a 66-metre vimana tower.

name: Amber Fort
description: A hilltop fort-palace near Jaipur built by Raja Man Singh I, blending Rajput and Mughal architectural elements across courtyards and mirrored halls.
significance: Part of the UNESCO-listed Hill Forts of Rajasthan and a major example of Rajput palace design.
indoor: Sheesh Mahal and palace museum halls

name: Hawa Mahal
description: A five-storey pink sandstone palace in Jaipur with 953 small latticed windows, built by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh to let royal women observe street life.
significance: An iconic example of Rajput honeycomb architecture and Jaipur's pink city identity.

name: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
description: A collection of nineteen astronomical instruments built by Maharaja Jai Singh II for observing celestial positions with the naked eye.
significance: The largest and best-preserved of India's historic observatories, reflecting advanced astronomical knowledge.

name: Rani ki Vav
description: An elaborately carved stepwell built by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband, King Bhima I, featuring seven levels of sculpted panels.
significance: Considered the finest and most intricately carved stepwell in India.

name: Dholavira
description: A major Harappan-era city on Khadir island featuring sophisticated water conservation systems, fortifications and planned urban layout.
significance: One of the largest and best-preserved Indus Valley Civilization sites, revealing early urban planning.

name: Elephanta Caves
description: Rock-cut cave temples on Elephanta Island near Mumbai, dedicated to Shiva and famed for the monumental Trimurti sculpture.
significance: A major centre of rock-cut religious art reflecting sophisticated sculptural traditions.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
description: A Victorian Gothic Revival railway terminus in Mumbai designed by F. W. Stevens, blending Indian and Victorian architectural traditions.
significance: A masterpiece of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture fused with traditional Indian building forms.
indoor: Heritage gallery within the station complex

name: Charminar
description: A monumental mosque-and-gateway structure built by Sultan Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, marking the founding of Hyderabad city.
significance: An iconic symbol of Hyderabad and a major example of Qutb Shahi Deccan architecture.

name: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib)
description: The holiest Gurdwara of Sikhism in Amritsar, with a sanctum sanctorum gilded in gold set amid a sacred pool, the Amrit Sarovar.
significance: The spiritual and architectural centre of Sikhism, renowned for its distinctive fusion of architectural styles.

name: Pattadakal Monuments
description: A group of Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chalukya dynasty, showcasing a fusion of northern (Nagara) and southern (Dravida) temple styles.
significance: A unique meeting point of North and South Indian temple architectural traditions.

name: Nalanda Mahavihara
description: The ruins of an ancient Buddhist monastic and scholastic institution that once attracted students from across Asia.
significance: One of the world's earliest great universities and a centre of Buddhist learning for over 700 years.

name: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya
description: A temple complex marking the site where Siddhartha Gautama is believed to have attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree.
significance: One of the four holiest sites of Buddhism and an early example of brick temple architecture.

name: Mysore Palace
description: The royal residence of the Wadiyar dynasty, rebuilt in Indo-Saracenic style by architect Henry Irwin after an earlier fire.
significance: One of India's most visited palaces and a striking example of Indo-Saracenic revival architecture.
sources: Karnataka Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage

name: Victoria Memorial
description: A grand white marble memorial in Kolkata built in honour of Queen Victoria, combining British and Mughal architectural elements.
significance: A landmark of colonial-era architecture and now a major museum of Indian history.
